blocks.text: 1. Prompt Construction

blocks.alt: A system prompt, context, and query combine into a final prompt

blocks.text: Prompt Construction covers how the final surviving context becomes an actual prompt, closing out the Context Management module by tying every earlier step together.
It closes the Context Management module by assembling every prior step's output into one finished prompt.
2. Every Step Lands Here
Budgeting, filtering, compression, ordering, and deduplication, covered in Context Deduplication and the steps before it, all shaped a final set of chunks.
Prompt construction turns that finished set into the literal text sent to the model.

blocks.text: 3. Template Structure For Consistency

blocks.alt: A prompt template gets filled with content

blocks.text: A consistent prompt template defines exactly where instructions, context, and the query each go.
That structure makes model behavior more predictable across every request.
4. Labeling Sources Within The Context

blocks.alt: A chunk carries a source label like doc.pdf page 3

blocks.text: As in Contextual Retrieval, where retrieval metadata gets attached to results, each included chunk can carry a visible source label in the prompt itself.
This lets the model reference or cite specific sources when it answers.
5. Separating Instructions From Retrieved Content

blocks.alt: Instructions are kept separate from retrieved content

blocks.text: Clear delimiters separate system instructions from the retrieved content itself.
This reduces the risk that the model confuses retrieved text for an actual instruction to follow.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A retrieved chunk that happens to contain text resembling an instruction could be misinterpreted as a command if not clearly delimited from actual system instructions, a real safety consideration in prompt construction.

blocks.text: 6. Placing The Query Itself
As covered in Lost-in-the-Middle Problem, the middle of long context gets less attention, so where the actual user query gets placed also affects how well the model attends to it.
Many templates deliberately place the query close to the end, right before the model responds.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Placing the user's actual question immediately before asking the model to respond leverages the same strong end of context attention covered in Lost-in-the-Middle Problem.

blocks.text: 7. Final Token Validation

blocks.alt: An assembled prompt goes through a token count check to verify it is within budget

blocks.text: As in Token Budgeting, where tokens are counted rather than characters, the fully assembled prompt needs one final token count check.
This catches any accumulated overflow before the request actually gets sent to the model.
8. Context Management As The Completed Pipeline
Every technique covered across this module fed into producing this one finished prompt.
This closes the Context Management module before Prompt Engineering for RAG, the next module, begins.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Careful Prompt Construction Matters Most

blocks.alt: A complex, multi-source prompt points toward constructing the prompt carefully

blocks.text: Production systems needing reliability and citations need careful prompt construction.
Quick prototypes with a single, simple context block, by contrast, can use a far simpler template.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates assembling a labeled, delimited prompt from the final surviving chunks.

code.content:
system_instructions = "You are a helpful support assistant. Cite sources using [source: X]."
final_chunks = [
    {"id": "handbook_v3", "text": "Refunds are processed within five business days."},
    {"id": "faq_page", "text": "Damaged items qualify for a full refund."},
]
user_query = "How long does a refund take for a damaged item?"

def construct_prompt(system_instructions, chunks, query):
    # builds a consistent template structure
    context_blocks = []
    for chunk in chunks:
        # labels each chunk with its source
        context_blocks.append(f"[source: {chunk['id']}] {chunk['text']}")
    context_section = "\n".join(context_blocks)

    # keeps instructions separated from retrieved content
    prompt = (
        f"### Instructions\n{system_instructions}\n\n"
        f"### Context\n{context_section}\n\n"
        f"### Question\n{query}"
    )
    return prompt

final_prompt = construct_prompt(system_instructions, final_chunks, user_query)
print("Final assembled prompt:\n")
print(final_prompt)

print(f"\nApproximate token count: {len(final_prompt.split())}")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the finished prompt organized into clearly delimited sections, with each chunk carrying its own source label and the query placed last.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Assembling context without a consistent template, producing unpredictable model behavior.
Omitting source labels, making it impossible for the model to cite where information came from.
Failing to delimit instructions from retrieved content, risking instruction confusion.
Skipping a final token count check on the fully assembled prompt before sending the request.

blocks.text: 12. Context Management: Module Complete

items: Context Window established the fixed capacity every other technique works within.
Token Budgeting covered allocating that finite space across every competing prompt component.
Context Compression covered shrinking selected chunks without losing needed information.
Context Filtering covered dropping chunks that fail a final relevance or quality check.
Context Ordering covered arranging surviving chunks for the best possible model attention.
Context Deduplication covered removing repeated information missed by earlier deduplication.
Prompt Construction closed the module by assembling everything into one finished prompt.
A consistent template, labeled sources, and clear delimiters all support reliable model behavior.
Next up: Prompt Engineering for RAG, covering how to write instructions that guide the model's response.
